findings.claim: Click's ANSI matcher only recognizes numeric parameters separated by semicolons.

evidence_receipt.claim: Click's ANSI matcher only recognizes numeric parameters separated by semicolons.
evidence_receipt.falsification_condition: The regex pattern includes a range [0-?]* which covers more than just numeric parameters separated by semicolons, thus contradicting the claim.

verification_result.stdout:
-_ansi_re = re.compile(r"\033\[[;?0-9]*[a-zA-Z]")
+# One CSI escape sequence per the ECMA-48 grammar: parameter bytes (0x30-0x3F),
+# intermediate bytes (0x20-0x2F), then a final byte (0x40-0x7E). Broader than the
+# SGR codes Click emits, so foreign sequences (colon-delimited true-color, mouse
+# reporting) are stripped too.
+_ansi_re = re.compile(r"\033\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]")

ground_truth_evidence: The updated regex uses the broader ECMA-48 byte ranges rather than the older numeric-only form.
